title: The Hiring Factory: How Great Companies Win the Best Talent — Book Launch + Talk
description:
Why would a candidate choose a $750,000 offer over one worth $1.5 million?

How did one recruiting change add 2,751 candidates to a company’s pipeline—while another caused more than 20,000 candidates to leave, costing the company 2,000 hires in five months?

These outcomes may appear unrelated. They aren’t.

Most companies don’t have a series of hiring problems. They have a system that keeps producing hiring problems.

Join author Ryan Silvers for the launch of The Hiring Factory, an upcoming book that examines hiring through the lens of economics, game theory, systems thinking, cybernetics, and AI.

In this talk, we’ll explore:

• Why some companies consistently attract and hire exceptional people while others struggle
• How to increase candidate response and maintain engagement throughout the process
• How to uncover and overcome the real reasons candidates hesitate, withdraw, or say no
• How to identify the hidden constraints causing a hiring system to repeatedly fail

You’ll also discover how the ideas that gave rise to AI can help us understand and redesign the systems companies use to hire.

Ryan Silvers has spent more than 15 years as an executive recruiter and recruiting leader at companies including AWS, Meta, and Atlassian.

title: Big Brain: Why Chimpanzees Can’t Give Lectures: The Evolution of Human Speech
description:
🗣️ Why can humans give speeches, while our closest primate relatives can’t speak the way we do?
​The answer does not begin with the mouth, or even the brain, but with a seemingly unrelated change in how our ancestors walked through the world. This talk traces the evolutionary journey that restructured the human respiratory system to make speech possible in the first place.
​Dr. Nkemdi Agwaramgbo, an internal medicine physician and hospitalist with a longstanding interest in human evolution, walks through the anatomy behind the human voice, from breath to whisper to lecture hall. Along the way, he explains why this same anatomy also makes humans uniquely vulnerable to choking, and how various diseases can disrupt our ability to speak.
​Agwaramgbo views anatomy and physiology not just as biological machinery, but as part of a larger story of what makes us human. His hope is to leave audiences with a humbling realization: speech was never guaranteed, and we are remarkably lucky to have it. 🫁

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

title: Strategy as an Emotional Act: An Interactive Practice for Changemakers #SFTechWeek
description:
We are living through rapid shifts in how we work, lead, relate, and make decisions. AI is accelerating some of those changes, but the deeper questions are human ones.

What do we want technology to make easier? What kinds of judgment, care, creativity, responsibility, and relationship do we want to protect? And how might the systems we build change when we treat those human capacities as part of the infrastructure, not as an afterthought?

In this interactive session, we’ll explore those questions through four elemental lenses: earth, water, fire, and air.

We’ll begin with a guided practice designed to help participants experience each element within themselves and notice the emotions, instincts, and ways of relating that emerge.

From there, participants will work in small groups to respond to a shared systems-change challenge. Each group will approach the same problem through a different elemental lens.

As we work, we’ll pay attention to how we feel, listen, disagree, influence one another, make decisions, and respond when different values or perspectives come into tension.

We’ll explore what becomes possible when a system is shaped by multiple ways of being rather than a single perspective.

You’ll leave with:

-A deeper language for understanding how emotion shapes decision-making and change

-Four practical lenses for recognizing different relational strengths, needs, and ways of solving problems

-Tools for creating healthier emotional and relational conditions within teams and organizations

Co-facilitated by Chelsea Borruano and Nima Imani.

Chelsea is a nonprofit founder, strategist, and facilitator whose work sits at the intersection of emotional awareness, organizational design, community-building, and systems change.

Nima is a founder and ICF-certified leadership coach who works with founders, leaders, and teams navigating uncertainty, difficult decisions, conflict, and the human side of change.

title: Post Generation | opening reception at TIAT
description:
Post Generation brings together three artists to transform an archive from early generative AI testing into new works of textile, media, and performance.

Bringing together textile artist Hayley Mortin (Montréal), media artist Karyn Nakamura (NYC), and performance artist Zelia ZZ Tan (LA), the exhibition presents three distinct interpretations of early AI’s strange, unstable, and unexpected outputs.

Created with support from Google, the artists were invited to draw from an extensive archive of videos produced during the testing of early Veo models. As generative video becomes increasingly polished, Post Generation looks back at the imaginative artifacts left behind and asks what new meanings artists might uncover within them.

₊˚✩ more on the artists

Hayley Mortin is a Montréal-based researcher and artist whose work connects human-centered AI, textile production, and independent publishing. She is a Staff UX Researcher specializing in AI, the founder of experimental knitwear project Dazy Chains, and the founding editor of Needlebound, an anthology documenting contemporary fibre culture.

Zelia ZZ Tan is a Los Angeles– and Hong Kong–based choreographer, director, media artist, and researcher exploring how bodies relate to technology and their environments through performance, motion capture, XR, and participatory systems. She is the co-founder of TechDanceLab, an Asian Cultural Council Altius Fellow, and holds MFAs in Choreography and Interactive Media for Performance from CalArts.

Karyn Nakamura is a Tokyo-born, New York–based artist and researcher whose work explores agency, communication, and honesty in technology through large-scale installations, moving image, and experimental systems. A graduate of MIT’s Art and Design program, she conducts visual forensics research with Northwestern University’s HAIC Lab and is a recipient of the Steve Jobs Archive Fellowship.

title: on being Chinese and online with viola he
description:

title: Critical Tea Theory: Gongfu Tea & Gongfu Uncles
description:
From D.T. Suzuki’s teachings on Zen Buddhism to tea ceremony and Daoist breathwork practices, Bay area counterculture in the 1960s took inspiration from Eastern esoteric traditions, responding to a profound disillusionment with Western modernity and late-stage capitalism with a desire for rituals of connection and slowness. Zen, yoga, and other contemplative traditions became central to the countercultural turn. The romance of the East has often furnished the most radical dreams of Western civilization’s discontents.

Now, on the brink of a new set of spiritual and political crises, Chinese civilization is appearing in the zeitgeist as a political, cultural and epistemological foil. What’s with the proliferation of social media footage of Chinese aunties and uncles performing wild calisthenic feats in public parks? Why is anime cool now? Why is everyone in a “very Chinese time of their life”? And why is there such a renewed interest in tea ceremony?

Join interdisciplinary artist and critical theorist Kelsey Chen (Stanford) for an experimental lecture and tea service to consider Chinamaxxing as an expression of the search for alternative epistemologies and the disillusionment with failing American institutions, thinking alongside tea as a central figure in the story of the complicated role that China has been enlisted to play historically and in this contemporary moment in Western political critique.

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

title: Fit Check: A Very Chinese Time in Your Wardrobe
description:
For centuries, the West dressed itself in fantasies of China: silk as a symbol of the far-away, jade as a mark of mystery, the qipao as an Orientalist costume. China was something to be borrowed, imitated, and worn, rarely something allowed to define itself.

Now, the internet is doing the defining. Grandma's padded jacket is a TikTok trend. Mamianqun skirts sell out on Taobao, red string bracelets show up in fit checks, and a jade bangle is equal parts heirloom, flex, and meme. Why does "very Chinese" now read as cool? Who decides what counts as Chinese fashion: the archive, the runway, or the comment section? And what happens to tradition when it travels through the algorithm and comes back as a vibe?

Join us for a share tracing Chinese fashion from tradition to memes, from heirloom craft to viral fits, and the playful experiences that are redefining what it means to dress Chinese today. title: Deep Listening - Good Grief by Sara Bareilles
description:
🎧 Deep Listening

🌿 About Event

When was the last time you gave yourself the luxury of dedicated listening to an album from beginning to end? Without multitasking, checking your phone, or doing anything else.

When was the last time you listened closely to the emotions and desires within you?

Deep Listening is an invitation to do both.

We’ll gather to listen to Sara Bareilles’ Good Grief in its entirety, setting aside the rare luxury of allowing music to monopolize our attention and wash over us. As we listen together, we’ll also turn our attention inward: to the feelings, memories, questions, and parts of ourselves that the music might bring to the surface.

Bring a journal and/or sketchbook as a place for whatever arises to take physical form. You can write, draw, doodle, or simply sit and listen. There’s nothing you need to produce, figure out, or share.

Our goal is to simply listen.

To notice what’s within us. To give it somewhere to land. To make space for something inside you that may not otherwise get heard.

And to do that in the presence of other people, but without any expectation to share or be vulnerable. My own experience has shown me the strength that becomes available to us when we turn inward while surrounded by others who are doing the same.

The first part of the gathering is intentionally gentle and private. Afterward, you’ll have the option to stay for a deeper experience of listening, reflection, and sharing in a small group.

You don’t need to come with a particular feeling in mind. You don’t need to consider yourself creative. You don’t need to know what you’re looking for.

Just bring yourself, something to write or draw with, and a curiosity for what you might discover.

🕰 Flow / Schedule

6:30-7pm · Arrive + Settle In
We’ll gather in a circle and begin with gentle movement, think of slow stretches that help us slow down, settle into our bodies, and become present to the experience ahead.

7-7:30pm · Deep Listening
We’ll listen to the first portion of Good Grief. Use your journal or sketchbook to write, draw, reflect, or simply listen.

7:30-8pm · Optional Sharing
A moment to share anything that surfaced with the wider group. Sharing is always optional.

8-8:30pm · Deeper Listening
We’ll listen to the second half of Good Grief. Similar to the first half, use your journal or sketchbook to write, draw, reflect, or simply listen.

8:30-9pm · Small Group Sharing + Closing

We’ll split into small groups for facilitated reflection and deeper sharing.

👥 Facilitator

Ran Ji created the community version of Deep Listening after experiencing the practice herself several times. Each time, she was surprised by the variety of the emotions, memories, and feelings that surfaced through simply listening to an album with her full attention.

She views art as a call and response: an artist puts something deeply personal into the world, and it calls to the parts of us that are ready to hear it. Her hope is to create a space where people can respond to that call with curiosity, privacy, and care.

Ran has been a teacher and tutor and has experience facilitating group discussions and helping people open up. More than anything, she brings a deep capacity to sit with people as they are in each moment, without requiring them to explain, perform, or move through their feelings on anyone else's timeline.

To learn more about Ran, visit her Instagram.

💫 Who This Is For

This space is for anyone who feels called to slow down and listen: to music, to themselves, and to what within might be asking for their attention.

You might be moving through grief or transition. You might be carrying something you don't have words for yet. Or you might simply want to spend an evening listening deeply and being in community.

No particular experience with journaling, drawing, meditation, or sharing is expected.

The sharing portions are entirely optional. You can participate as privately as you'd like.

You’re also always welcome to step outside, take a break, or leave if you need to.

Builders Night is a weekly space where people show up with a project, work side by side, and leave with more momentum than they could have generated alone. It exists because building can be lonely, and the hardest part is often simply showing up consistently.

Who This Is For

People working on software, hardware, businesses, creative projects, writing, design, research, art, anything you're trying to make real. Come if you want accountability, momentum, and the energy of working alongside others. First-timers and regulars both welcome.

What to Bring

Laptop, notebook, sketchbook, instrument, whatever tools your project requires. Come with something to work on, or come ready to figure out what that is.

Norms

Respect the deep work sprint by keeping conversation low during focused time. Share-back is how we learn from each other: share what you built, ask for what you need, and offer what you can. Everyone participates.

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

Our guest curator this month is Rachel Heleva, a game designer and researcher, and Executive Director of the MADE.

What happens when a poem becomes something you can play? When rules, choices, repetition, chance, constraint, and computation become part of how a poem makes meaning? And from the other direction, when does a game begin to behave like a poem?

Game Poems brings together writers, artists, and game makers working between poetry and play for an evening of short readings, performances, demonstrations, and works in progress. We’ll encounter games made from language, poems structured by rules, computational literature, interactive fiction, and other forms that trouble the boundary between reading and playing.

Rachel will also share a prototype of In Countless Shadows, which treats Shakespeare’s sonnets as playable systems.

The presentations will be followed by a conversation facilitated by Helen Shewolfe Tseng.

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

title: Thirst Draft: Write Drunk, Edit Never
description:
An event for writers — and for writing. Everyone gets the same prompt when they walk in the door. What ends up on the page is up to you!
Here’s how it works:
Write whatever you want — poem, song, short story, joke… anything works!
Interpret the prompt however you like, but try to incorporate it in some way
Work alone or collaborate with friends/strangers — no word count or time limit
Sign up by 7pm if you want to share your piece on stage, just like an open mic
Want to join, but can’t make it by 6 pm? All good!
Here are some loose times to keep in mind:
Write & Mingle: 6pm to 7pm
Share on Stage: 7pm to 8pm
Drink & Discuss: 8pm to 9pm
No cover, no editing, no AI. Pens and paper will be available, but bring your own if you can. Tip your bartenders and support your fellow writers.
